title: Normalized pullback counit shift square on K-flat representatives
statement: Let f:Z→Y be a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] of Noetherian schemes with recorded derived categories [def-pc-derived-category] in a common localization universe. Let F=Lf* be derived pullback [def-pc-derived-pullback] with a supplied strong monoidal structure [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure], and let H be the homotopy functor induced by additive termwise tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. Write Qh_X for localization and c_X(K):O_X[1]⊗K≅K[1] for the canonical shift-unit comparison [def-sc-scheme-canonical-shift-unit-iso]. Fix a natural transformation ε₀:Qh_Y⋙F→H⋙Qh_Z invertible at each K-flat representative [def-pc-kflat-complex]. There exist an isomorphism e:F(O_Y[1])≅O_Z[1] and a natural transformation ε:Qh_Y⋙F→H⋙Qh_Z, invertible at every K-flat representative. Put G=H⋙Qh_Z. For every K-flat cochain complex P, with X its image in the homotopy category, ε(X[1])≫commShift_G(X) equals F(commShift_Qh_Y(X))≫b(Qh_Y(X))≫ε(X)[1], where b(K) is F(c_Y(K) inverse), followed by the supplied inverse tensorator at (O_Y[1],K), e tensor identity, and c_Z(F(K)). The assertion is only on K-flat representatives and makes no claim about a factorization against ε₀ or about cone maps.

proof.text: Construct e and the natural isomorphism family α only on K-flat homotopy representatives and their one-fold translates using [lem-sc-normalized-kflat-representative-comparison]. The choices are joint; no square for arbitrary e is asserted.

Every homotopy object is the image of a complex. Apply [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] and take the quotient of its quasi-isomorphism. Its source belongs to the representative class. Qh inverts these quasi-isomorphisms, so Qh⋙derivedPullback does too; the quasi-isomorphisms have the Mathlib right fraction calculus. Apply [lem-sc-nattrans-from-resolving-class] to α.hom to obtain ε agreeing with α on the class.

At q(P) and q(P)[1], rewrite ε using its agreement with α. The first equality gives invertibility since α is an isomorphism. The second and first together rewrite the desired shift square into the representative shift square.
